- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate downward trend; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to counteract bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., > 0.3 for 3+ consecutive days), model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 5–7 days.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 2–5 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–3 days ahead of actual shift.
